title: Flight surgeon gum exam, burns and skin samples while OSI watched
place_text: Flight surgeon's office, Ellsworth AFB, South Dakota

tellings.quote: you know you have a couple of burns on your body right and I said excuse me he goes yeah above your right eye and on the back of your right hand
He went up here and he just clipped a piece of skin off there and he took the whole tool and he stuck it right down in there and put a cork on it, laid it on that tray.
tellings.difference: Describes the skin being clipped and corked in a tube on the tray.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe the flight surgeon taking skin samples from Mario at Ellsworth in 1977 while OSI watched.

as_told.title: Flight surgeon takes a skin tissue sample from Mario

tellings.quote: The next day, I returned to Ellsworth and was interviewed by the 44th Missile Wing commander. There was a guy in civilian clothing with him who I think was from the [Office of Special Investigations].

Then I was also ordered to take a urinalysis at the base hospital, and two skin samples were taken—one from the back of my right hand and another above my right eyebrow—as I was sunburned for some strange reason.

plain: After his 1977 encounter at a nuclear missile site, Mario Woods says an Air Force flight surgeon at Ellsworth Air Force Base examined him, found burns, and took skin samples while investigators looked on. Woods, a former missile security guard, tells Michels the doctor said, "you have a couple of burns on your body", "above your right eye and on the back of your right hand". In a later telling he describes the doctor clipping "a piece of skin off", sticking the tool in a tube "and put a cork on it, laid it on that tray". He says agents of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations, the Air Force's own investigative service, were watching. The researcher Robert Hastings published Woods's written account on 10 September 2017. There Woods says he was interviewed "the next day" by the 44th Missile Wing commander, with "a guy in civilian clothing" he thought was from that office. He writes that he was ordered to take a urine test at the base hospital and that "two skin samples were taken", from "the back of my right hand and another above my right eyebrow", "as I was sunburned for some strange reason". If true, the Air Force would have taken and kept physical evidence from the encounter.
